description.narrative: The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to: (i) improve the timeliness and availability of information to support the delivery and management of public health services; and (ii) to foster the development and roll-out of eHealth applications and services, and Information and Communication Technology (ICT) services more generally.

The development objective of the eGabon Project for Gabon is to: (i) improve the timeliness and availability of information to support the delivery and management of public health services; and (ii) to foster the development and roll-out of eHealth applications and services, and Information and Communication Technology (ICT) services more generally. It comprises the following three components. The first component, strengthening the National Health Information System (NHIS) is to improve the timeliness and availability of information to support health service delivery and management which should contribute to improving Gabon's human development outcomes. The NHIS should lead to improved accountability and work productivity for the health professionals, both in terms of reducing the administrative burden for health care workers, and minimizing administrative and medical errors. It will significantly change the way in which health workers deliver care, especially those in rural areas where clinicians will have easier access to relevant specialists in urban areas, who would be available for any needed consultation. Electronic medical records and ePrescribing, together with clinical decision support capability, should allow clinical staff to improve both diagnosis and treatment, and reduce medical and prescribing mistakes due to illegible handwriting or unclear abbreviations on hand-written notes. Improved diagnosis and treatment should reduce the incidence of unnecessary hospitalization and lessen the financial burden on the poor. The quality of data available to inform management decision-making would similarly improve, since much of it would be collected in real-time as part of the clinical encounter; The second component, advancing the digital innovation ecosystem development is to contribute to Gabon's economic diversification by fostering the emergence of a digital innovation ecosystem. This will include the development of a digital incubator in Libreville and smaller-scale incubators in Port-Gentil and Franceville, and should have the side benefit of improving both private and public e-service delivery, which will be critical to generate new entrepreneurship opportunities, in particular for women and youth. The incubators will be leveraged to promote a particular focus on health applications, including contributions to the development of the NHIS (Component 1), and mHealth, and other ICT-based innovations for health. This will impact health outcomes as well as economic development; The third component, project management, coordination, monitoring and evaluation of the project is to provide fiduciary support to the Project by the National Commission – Labor Intensive Small-Scale Public Infrastructure Works (CN-TIPPEE) , building upon the arrangements set up for the Central African Backbone SOP4, Gabon Project (CAB4). This component will support the Borrower in the areas of Project coordination, supervision, financial management, procurement, monitoring and evaluation, communication, audits, and preparation and supervision of implementation of the safeguard instruments, preparation of related surveys, including through the provision of training, operating costs, goods and services for the required purpose.

Targeted hospitals and medical centers provided with information technology equipment (PC and Servers) to facilitate interconnection and NHIS operation

comment.narrative: This indicator was introduced during the second restructuring (August 2022). All 13 targeted health facilities were equipped with the IT infrastructure required to operate the NHIS (100% coverage). In addition, seven further facilities benefited from equipment provision, laying a strong foundation for future expansion.

title.narrative: Targeted hospitals and medical centers with cabling infrastructure installed to facilitate intercommunication

comment.narrative: This indicator was introduced during the second restructuring (August 2022). The targeted sites were the 13 health facilities selected for NHIS deployment. The project supported network cabling works in all 13 pilot facilities, as well as in an additional seven health facilities and one health training institution. In ISR No. 17 (December 2025), this resulted in a reported achievement of 21 out of 13 (162%). However, since the denominator was fixed at the 13 targeted sites, the achievement rate should be capped at 100%. Accordingly, the achievement is reported here as 100%, reflecting full coverage of all targeted facilities. At the same time, the extension of network cabling to eight additional sites should be highlighted, as it lays an important foundation for the future expansion of the NHIS beyond the project scope after closure.

title.narrative: Targeted hospitals and medical centers information technology personnel trained with skills to operate and maintain the NHIS

comment.narrative: This indicator was introduced during the third restructuring (August 2025). At project closing, all target sites had personnel equipped with the skills to operate and maintain the NHIS. These consist of permanent IT staff in some sites and trained interns from Gabon's Nkok IT School in others.

title.narrative: NHIS support services (accounting, reception...) level of satisfaction with the efficiency of the NHIS

comment.narrative: A survey of support services staff conducted in March 2026 found that 66.3% were satisfied with the system (on a Likert scale: ‘Highly satisfied’ or ‘Satisfied’). While this is below the 80% target, the result is encouraging, as the system had only recently been rolled out in several sites, users are still becoming familiar with it, and further system improvements were ongoing at the time of the survey. Another 21.2% of respondents reported being neutral, suggesting that only a limited share expressed dissatisfaction (‘Unsatisfied’ or ‘Highly unsatisfied’).

comment.narrative: Beyond health workers and participants in hackathons and training courses organized by the incubator, beneficiaries of the e-Gabon project are estimated to include all potential patients in the municipalities targeted by the deployment of the National Health Information System (NHIS). This definition is consistent with the original PAD. The indicator target was revised during the 2022 project restructuring, decreasing from 1,820,000 to 900,000 as the scope of deployment was geographically limited to Greater Libreville (the municipalities of Libreville, Owendo, and Akanda). The project deployed the NHIS across 13 health facilities in the municipalities of Libreville, Owendo, and Akanda. Based on 2022 demographic projections, the combined population of the three municipalities is estimated at 1,067,185, indicating that the revised target (900,000) has been surpassed.

title.narrative: Selected hospitals with NHIS installed and operational

comment.narrative: This indicator was introduced during the second restructuring (August 2022). At project closing, the National Health Information System (NHIS) has been deployed across all 13 selected health facilities, including university hospital centers, military hospitals, cooperation hospitals, and health centers in Greater Libreville.

Component 2 of the project, focused on advancing the digital innovation ecosystem, was completed in 2022. At that time, 53 start-up projects had been incubated by SING - an incubator established with support from the project - thus exceeding the target of 50. The project continued to monitor this indicator even after the closure of Component 2. By project closing, a total of 139 start-ups had been incubated. This figure is reported here as it provides valuable evidence of the sustainability and long-term impact of SING's activities.

title.narrative: Health workers level of satisfaction regarding the effectiveness of NHIS
Health workers reporting that they regularly use and update the patients electronic medical record during clinical consultations

comment.narrative: This indicator was initially designed to be measured through an annual health worker survey but is now based on NHIS system-generated data. The methodology calculates the share of registered users who recorded at least one clinical action during the reference month. While this constitutes a major methodological change, it enhances objectivity and allows for continuous updates. Results from ISR 17 (December 2025) are not comparable. At project closure, 1,173 of 2,769 registered users recorded at least one action, resulting in a usage rate of 42.4%. While below target, this reflects the recent rollout of the NHIS across all 13 sites and early-stage adoption. The estimate may also be affected by data quality issues, including the presence of inactive user accounts (e.g., accounts of health workers who left their facilities), which may inflate the denominator. A positive trend is observed, with usage increasing from 34% in March 2026, suggesting continued growth as the system stabilizes.

title.narrative: Health workers level of satisfaction regarding the effectiveness of NHIS

comment.narrative: A survey of health workers conducted in March 2026 found that 66.7% were satisfied with the system (on a Likert scale: ‘Highly satisfied’ or ‘Satisfied’). While this is below the 80% target, the result is highly encouraging, as the system had only recently been rolled out in several sites, users are still becoming familiar with it, and further system improvements were ongoing at the time of the survey. Another 19.75% of respondents reported being neutral, implying that only a limited share expressed dissatisfaction (‘Unsatisfied’ or ‘Highly unsatisfied’)

title.narrative: Estuaire region (province) hospitals interconnected to host the NHIS

comment.narrative: At the time of the third restructuring (August 2025), the Estuaire region had 20 health facilities, of which 13 were retained under the revised project scope. The target was adjusted to 75 percent, although this appears miscalculated, as 13 out of 20 corresponds to 65 percent. The project successfully interconnected all 13 targeted facilities. Following the closure of one facility, the total decreased to 19, resulting in a final ratio of 68.4 percent. While this falls short of the 75 percent target, the gap reflects the initial mis-specification of the target, as the project achieved its planned scope. A previous ISR reported 100 percent for this indicator, as it referred only to the 13 pilot sites rather than all facilities in the region.

title.narrative: Information technology managers and technicians trained

comment.narrative: There was a mix-up in this indicator's value in the previous ISR. The previous figure (166) was erroneously entered, and represented the healthcare professionals trained, not the technicians. Training began in 2022 within healthcare facilities with 70 participants; In 2024, 3 additional people received ICT training, bringing the cumulative number of Information Technology Managers and Technicians trained to 73 as of March 2025.

title.narrative: Completion of business process re-engineering and change management activities

comment.narrative: Operational and change management processes were implemented in four phases, each with a defined set of activities. Based on the average completion rate across phases - 100% for Phase 1, 85% for Phase 2, 100% for Phase 3, and 85% for Phase 4 - the overall completion rate reached 92.5%, indicating that the target was achieved.
